subject: English
passage: The European earthworm and other detritivore species introduced to Canadian boreal forest regions in the last 200 years have recently been found to decompose leaf litter from native forest trees that are at risk of decline, such as the black spruce. Many of these vulnerable tree species rely on the activity of decomposer organisms to help process organic matter and cycle nutrients in forest soils. Native earthworm species in these forests have largely disappeared, suggesting that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: European earthworms and other non-native organisms play an important role that used to be filled by species that were native to these forests.
choices.B: non-native organisms, such as the European earthworm, will also be at risk of decline if they lose access to black spruce trees.
choices.C: populations of European earthworms and other non-native organisms will probably soon experience rapid growth.
choices.D: non-native organisms, such as the European earthworm, now decompose more leaf litter from black spruce trees than native species did in the past.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of decomposer organisms in Canadian boreal forests. The text establishes that introduced organisms decompose leaf litter from native trees, that vulnerable trees rely on decomposer activity for nutrient cycling, and that native earthworm species have largely disappeared. Since native decomposers are gone but trees still need decomposers to survive, non-native organisms must now fill the ecological role that native species once held.
